v: Nithiin is back on the HIT track! The organic-farming message takes a back seat to comedy, but once the second half lets loose, the punches and performances make this a pakka commercial entertainer.
e: Bheeshma uses organic farming as its plot foundation but Venky Kudumula keeps the message secondary to entertainment. The first half is okay, the post-interval comedy lifts the film considerably, and Nithiin, Vennela Kishore, Raghu Babu and the stylish presentation make it an easy commercial watch if you leave logic at the door.
body:
Nithiin is back again on the HIT track!!!

Plot-wise, the concept of organic farming is almost kicked aside by director Venky Kudumula’s narration style.

It is interesting how differently directors can approach the same kind of subject. If this plot had been handled by someone like Koratala Siva, it could easily have become a commercially serious, message-oriented film with stylish action scenes. Venky chooses a completely different route and mixes entertainment into the message-heavy setup.

The message is almost dominated by the comedy, but for a general entertainment-loving audience that is not necessarily a bad thing.

The first half was okay. With the interval twist, I actually thought the second half would turn serious and that all the hype about the comedy was going to be a bluff.

But the immediate post-interval scene makes the director’s intention very clear — he is not leaving the comedy angle at all — and that is where the real fun starts!!!!!

The one-liners, punches and even those intentionally irritating meme-style lines given to Nithiin are well written. Raghu Babu and Vennela Kishore together rock to the core!!!!

The movie is also shot quite stylishly. The BGM works, there are a couple of hit songs and the fights are good.

Surprisingly, the songs do not give Nithiin too many chances to show off his dancing, and in the only proper mass number Rashmika ends up taking most of the attention 😄

Overall, this is a pakka commercial entertainer with plenty of comedy in the second half, where the hero can happily do all the buffoonery and still remain the HERO!!!

Do not enter expecting a serious message or too much logic, and you are likely to enjoy it.

v: Excellent!!!!! Simple, realistic and refreshingly free of melodrama. Kangana is superb, the supporting cast clicks, and this is a MUST WATCH — theatre or OTT, the sooner the better!!!
e: Panga takes a story that could easily have been pushed into loud melodrama and tells it with wonderful simplicity and realism instead. Ashwiny Iyer Tiwari gets the emotions right, Kangana Ranaut is superb, and the entire supporting cast helps turn it into an effortless must-watch.
body:
Excellent!!!!!

How do you make a movie with this kind of story in such a simple and realistic way, without falling into unnecessary melodrama?

For me, there was hardly a scene that felt unrealistic. Director Ashwiny Iyer Tiwari does a fantastic job of getting the emotions right without forcing them.

We already know Kangana Ranaut is a fantastic and natural actor, but man, she is a SUPER STAR 🙏

She portrays all the emotions of a housewife carrying an unfinished dream in a wonderfully natural way.

And it is not just Kangana. Jassie Gill, Richa Chadha and Neena Gupta all do their jobs perfectly.

Special mention also to the kid playing the son — he fits into the family beautifully and adds a lot of warmth to the film.

The music and BGM blend perfectly with the mood, while the dialogues stay simple yet make complete sense.

Whether you watch it in a theatre or later on OTT, this is a MUST WATCH.

The sooner, the better!!!

v: Neither good nor bad — just above average. The sci-fi idea, retro setup, Sunil and Thaman create interest, but Ravi Teja’s energy overwhelms the concept until the film starts feeling routine.
e: Disco Raja throws sci-fi, retro styling and regular mass cinema into the same mixer, but Vi Anand never fully balances the concept with Ravi Teja’s trademark energy. There are interesting ingredients — especially Sunil’s return and Thaman’s terrific music and BGM — yet the film ultimately lands only a little above average.
body:
Personally, I feel Disco Raja is almost Vi Anand’s version of iSmart Shankar — sci-fi and regular mass cinema thrown together into one mixer!!!!!

The biggest challenge with Ravi Teja is that a director has to decide how much to use his energy levels and comedy timing.

If you do not use them enough, a section of the audience may feel the movie is slow and dull.

But if you use them too much, Ravi Teja can take over the entire film with his high energy and push the concept and story into the background.

And that is where I felt Vi Anand failed to find the right balance.

The sci-fi concept, the retro setup and the re-introduction of Sunil all create genuine interest.

But once Ravi Teja arrives in full Disco Raja mode, his energy overshadows almost everything around him, and that is when the movie starts feeling routine despite the unusual setup.

Apart from Ravi Teja, the two things that grabbed my attention most were Thaman’s terrific music and BGM and Sunil 🙏

There is enough style and novelty in the ingredients to keep it from becoming a bad film, but the execution never turns those ingredients into something truly special.

Overall, it is neither a good nor a bad movie — just above average!!!

v: A wafer-thin, predictable family story that I still liked to the core! Trivikram’s comedy and emotions, Allu Arjun, Murali Sharma and Thaman turn it into a simple, cool entertainer.
e: Ala Vaikunthapurramuloo reveals its basic story almost immediately, yet Trivikram keeps the film engaging through comedy, family emotions and strong character work. Allu Arjun gets a full showcase, Murali Sharma is a terrific second pillar, and Thaman’s chartbusters and BGM give this simple commercial film plenty of life.
body:
Very rarely do you see a film where you cannot point to one single outstanding element, yet you still like the film to the core — a little like Seethamma Vakitlo Sirimalle Chettu for me.

Ala Vaikunthapurramuloo falls into that category.

You can understand the basic story within the first ten minutes, but Trivikram’s command over comedy and family emotions, Murali Sharma’s excellent characterisation and acting, and Allu Arjun’s all-round performance keep you engaged for the entire length.

Because the family story itself is wafer-thin, Trivikram does not get as much space to show the kind of intellectual dialogue brilliance we saw in films such as Aravinda Sametha, Julayi or Khaleja.

Even then, his pen keeps moving, with a few trademark Trivikram lines scattered throughout the film.

Allu Arjun is back with a bang!!!

He gets a brilliant opportunity to handle comedy, emotion, mass fights and class fights in a single movie. And once again, he proves why he is among the best dancers in Tollywood — those trademark graceful steps look simple until you imagine trying to perform them yourself 🙏

Special mention to the dance episode in the office boardroom. It creates the kind of instant crowd impact that reminded me of Gabbar Singh’s antakshari scene, while cleverly giving PK fans their little ego-satisfaction moment too 😄

Trivikram and the fight masters also make sure the action portions are staged with conviction.

And unlike Agnyaathavaasi and Aravinda Sametha, this time Trivikram takes extra care not to spoil the impact of the chartbuster songs with their picturisation. The lead-in scenes, locations and sets blend nicely with the songs.

On screen, if Allu Arjun is one pillar, Murali Sharma is the other.

His characterisation and performance create exactly the impact required for us to dislike him throughout the film.

Apart from Murali Sharma and Sachin Khedekar, though, many of the other star actors are used more or less like junior artists 😦

Thaman gives the movie enormous life with his chartbuster songs and ultra-cool BGM.

Overall, this is a simple, cool commercial film that worked very well for me, especially as an Allu Arjun and Murali Sharma showcase.

The story may be familiar and predictable, but the entertainment around it makes the ride worthwhile.
